title: The Architect of Small Repairs

protagonist.name: Debabrata Sen
protagonist.role: Retired structural draughtsman, Dover Lane, Kolkata
protagonist.coreConflict: The belief that broken human relationships can be maintained through physical craftsmanship, avoiding words until time runs out.

counterpart.name: Ritwik Sen
counterpart.role: Urban architect, Singapore; Debabrata's only son
counterpart.dynamic: The modern architect who views his father's devotion to an old house as stubborn stagnation, yet carries the same inability to apologize.

setting.primary: The two-storey ancestral brick house on Dover Lane, Ballygunge
setting.secondary: The rear garage workshop with seasoned teak planks; the inner courtyard under the guava tree
setting.atmosphere: Fragrant wood shavings, raw linseed oil, the rhythmic scraping of a Japanese hand plane, the oppressive humidity of late October

signatureObjects: The Japanese kanna hand-plane brought by Debabrata's father from Burma in 1948
The creaking floorboard outside Ritwik's childhood bedroom that sounded an F-sharp
The grandmother's cedar dowry chest with a split lid joined by three rosewood butterfly dovetails
structuralMilestones: Ritwik's arrival with a property developer's power-of-attorney deed
Debabrata's quiet refusal to debate, offering instead a joint project: fixing the swollen library door
Working together in the garage: the tactile rhythm of wood, chisel, and square
The confrontation over the cedar chest and the real reason Ritwik left ten years ago
The completed repair that does not save the house, but saves father and son
